[T3 Code: this message came through T3 Code's tools, not from the user typing in this chat.]

Fix the HTML mail reader's failures on macOS WKWebView, found in the owner's macOS check for PR #92 (HTML mail reader, ADR 0006, merged to main; see the "Owner action: macOS check" section via `gh pr view 92`). The check ran on main at 59e5dfb with `pnpm tauri dev` and the default fixture profile. Results: steps 1, 3, 4 pass; 2, 5, 6, 7 fail.

## Main bug (steps 5, 6, 7): parent-attached listeners never run inside the mail frame on WebKit

`src/components/HtmlMessageFrame.vue` renders mail in a `srcdoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` (no `allow-scripts`), then the parent attaches listeners to the frame's document (around lines 148-152): `doc.addEventListener('click', …, true)`, `doc.addEventListener('keydown', …, true)` and `img.addEventListener('load', fit)`.

WebKit refuses to run any event listener whose target document is in a sandboxed frame without `allow-scripts`, even when the listener function belongs to the parent realm. Chromium (and so the Android WebView) runs them. That's why Android passed and macOS fails. Evidence from the Web Inspector console on macOS:
- A test listener added from the parent with `frame.contentDocument.addEventListener('click', …, true)` ran 0 times after a dispatched click. The same listener on the parent `document` ran once.
- Each blocked call logs "Blocked script execution in 'about:srcdoc' because the document's frame is sandboxed and the 'allow-scripts' permission is not set."
- Parent-side DOM APIs on the frame still work (`contentDocument.querySelector`, setting `img.src`, reading layout). Only listeners are blocked.

User-visible effects on macOS:
- Step 5: clicking an https link or a `mailto:` link in conv-20 does nothing. There's no confirmation dialog and no New message.
- Step 6: after clicking inside a message, the frame has focus and `j`/`k` do nothing, because the keydown forwarder never runs. With focus outside the frame, `j`/`k` work.
- Image `load` → `fit` never fires, so height fitting relies only on the ResizeObserver path.
- Step 7: `FRAME_PROBE_SOURCE` in `tests/rendered/html-frame-probe.ts` gives 36 PASS and 1 FAIL. The FAIL is "remote image blocked by CSP — [], width=0". Its `securitypolicyviolation` listener is attached to the frame document from the parent, so it never runs on WebKit. WebKit's own console report shows the CSP did block the image ("Refused to load https://probe-image.invalid/p.png because it does not appear in the img-src directive"). Every no-script check passed.

Constraints:
- Do NOT add `allow-scripts` or any other sandbox token. ADR 0006 decision 9 forbids it, and the no-script guarantee and fail-closed Tauri-global guard must keep holding.
- Keep text selection and copy inside the message working, along with keyboard link activation (Enter/Space on a link) and the per-link confirmation flow.
- Behaviour on Chromium/Android must not regress.

Design the fix (record it in the ADR's implementation record if it changes the approach), implement it with focused tests, and make the probe's CSP check work on WebKit without weakening it, e.g. a signal that doesn't depend on a listener inside the frame.

## Secondary issues

1. Step 2 (conv-21 inline logo is invisible on macOS): `crates/mail-core/src/synthetic/html/logo.png.b64` is a corrupt PNG, because its IDAT chunk CRC is wrong. The stored CRC is `ef bf 6b db` and the correct one is `ef a2 a7 5b`. The `ef bf` looks like a UTF-8 replacement-character mangling, so check how the file was produced. The corrected base64 is `iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mP8/x8AAwMCAO+ip1sAAAAASUVORK5CYII=`. Chromium ignores chunk CRCs, but Apple ImageIO decodes the file as fully transparent. Swapping in the corrected bytes in the live DOM made the white 64×64 logo show, so the cid pipeline itself works. Fix the fixture and check that nothing else (the same bytes are decoded in `crates/mail-core/src/synthetic/provider.rs` around lines 240 and 383, plus any TS fixture copies, tests or golden sizes such as "68 B") depends on the old bytes. A small test that validates fixture PNG CRCs would stop this coming back.
2. Step 1 cosmetic: after Load images, failed remote images in conv-19 render square on WebKit (the 600×220 header became 600×600), because `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }` in `src/lib/html-mail/frame-document.ts` loses the width/height aspect ratio for broken images. It's low priority; fix it only if it's cheap and safe.

## Notes

- This sandbox can't run WKWebView, so you can't reproduce the WebKit behaviour here. Reason from the evidence above, and test with the rendered suites in Chrome plus unit tests. Where you can't verify on WebKit, write down exactly what the owner must recheck on the Mac.
- Follow the repo's AGENTS/CLAUDE conventions and run the relevant checks.
- Commit to this branch. Before you push or open a PR, report back with a summary of the design, the diff and the test results.

# Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: a durable
synthetic fixture profile and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages. Slice 01
describes the fixture baseline; the current core also includes Gmail OAuth, cache,
sync, and provider operations.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
Fixture mode (the Gmail core on the built-in synthetic provider) has the same read/star
controls and cached Starred view, shown by the backend's explicit capability. Reminders use
local device storage in both native profiles. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
UX-06 adds one durable local
sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.

## Layout

| Path | Owner |
|---|---|
| `crates/mail-core/` | Rust DTOs, fixture core, Gmail provider/auth/cache/sync/actions, SQLite, profile locks |
| `src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`, configs | Vue 3/TypeScript frontend, IPC adapter and tests |
| `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` | **Generated** — do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run gen:ts` |
| `src-tauri/` | Thin Tauri 2 shell: typed mail/draft/close commands, `mailbox_changed` and `drafts_changed` hints, fixture/Gmail profile selection and lifecycle |
| `mise.toml` | Project tasks (see below) |

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
Catalog and page rows are real buttons with one roving tab stop: ArrowDown/ArrowUp
or J/K move between rows, Enter opens, and Escape steps back one level (reader,
page list, catalog) before it closes the drawer. Errors use the same plain
sentences as the Account drawer, never a raw error kind.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. This increment preserves
and coexists with the current UX-06/07/08 implementations. See
[the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)
for evidence and remaining gates.

## Tooling

All commands run through [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) (pinned: node 24.4.1,
pnpm 10.18.0, rust 1.89.0 with `rustfmt` and `clippy`). First-time setup:

```sh
mise trust           # after inspecting the repository's mise.toml
mise install         # install the project-pinned runtimes/tools
mise run setup:linux  # Debian/Ubuntu VMs only; installs OS packages with apt-get
mise run install:ui   # locked frontend dependencies (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile)
```

The Rust entry in `mise.toml` selects the minimal toolchain profile and explicitly
installs `rustfmt` and `clippy`, so a fresh `mise install` supplies both lint tools.
CI pins the mise installer action and mise version; it uses the same tool declaration.
Verify with `mise exec -- cargo fmt --version` and `mise exec -- cargo clippy --version`.

Rust dependencies resolve via the committed `Cargo.lock` on first `cargo`/`mise` use;
no global configuration is needed.

### Android fixture APK

The Android target is a fixture-only Tauri app with a viewport-driven compact phone shell
(up to 719 CSS px); browser preview uses the same layout mode. It uses the same synthetic fixture core
and SQLite profile as native fixture mode (ADR 0002). Android always selects fixture mode,
even if `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail` is present. A pre-existing legacy fixture database is retired
once behind the startup screen (closing the app is the cancel path). Gmail account controls and attachment export are unavailable on Android. The shell returns
the typed `unsupported_platform` error for attachment export. Confirmed external links dispatch through an Android ACTION_VIEW intent via JNI. The WebView
content remains padded for safe system insets; native status and navigation bars use the app
surface color and light icons. Compact layout keeps the existing capabilities and adds no mail
engine or IPC behavior. See [ADR 0003](adr/0003-mobile-layout.md) and [UX-14](ux-14-mobile-shell.md).

The current repeatable build lane targets Linux x86_64. Install JDK 17, Android
command-line tools, platform API 35, build-tools 35.0.0, and NDK 27.2.12479018.
The project Android template pins the same NDK version. The SDK root defaults to
`$HOME/Android/Sdk`; set `ANDROID_HOME`,
`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, `NDK_HOME`, and `JAVA_HOME` when your paths differ. Install
the SDK packages and Rust targets with:

```sh
"$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager" \
  "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" "ndk;27.2.12479018"
rustup target add aarch64-linux-android x86_64-linux-android
```

Use `mise run android:doctor` to check the local prerequisites. Then build one
debug APK containing ARM64 and x86_64 native libraries:

```sh
mise run android:build
```
## Owner action: macOS check (about 15 minutes)

This VM cannot run WKWebView. On the Mac, run `pnpm tauri dev` on this branch with the native fixture profile:

1. Open `conv-19` (newsletter). It fits the column and the "Remote images blocked." bar shows. Load images shows alt text or broken images (the hosts are `.invalid`) and nothing else changes.
2. Open `conv-21`. The inline logo shows without Load images.
3. Open `conv-22`. The quoted part is collapsed, and Show quoted text opens it.
4. Open `conv-23` (hostile). The window title stays "email-os", no dialog appears and the text shows. The message is **not** replaced by "Formatted view unavailable".
5. Click a link in `conv-20`. The confirmation shows the full URL, Copy link works and Keep reading closes it. Click the `mailto:` link: New message opens with only To filled.
6. Click inside a message, then press `j`/`k`. Navigation still works.
7. Open the Web Inspector and select the app page. Paste `FRAME_PROBE_SOURCE` from `tests/rendered/html-frame-probe.ts` into the console and run it. Every line should be `PASS`. This repeats the no-script proof on WKWebView. The console should otherwise show only CSP reports for blocked images.

Report the results in words. As an option, open three or four real newsletters with an explicit Gmail profile and report in words; no real mail is committed.

## Open items

- **Launch ANR on Android.** The app often gives "Input dispatching timed out … Waited 5001ms for FocusEvent" at launch on this emulator: three times on 21 November, and with the `db9f07e` APK on the first launch and again on a later one, at load averages of about 1 to 3. Other launches were clean. This PR adds startup work once per profile (schema migration 10 and the fixture seed upgrade). I have not compared against a `main` build, so the cause is not established. Startup is track A's.
- **macOS WKWebView is unverified** until the owner check above.
- **Shared files with other tracks.**
  - Track A (package rename, startup): `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (CSP), `src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json`, `src/App.vue`.
  - Track D (send): `src/composables/useDrafts.ts` (`openNew` takes optional initial content), `src/App.vue`, `src/components/ReaderView.vue`.

  Whichever merges second rebases. If track A renames the package first, this branch is rebased and the Android checks repeated.
- **Process deviation.** Sub-agents wrote the code for each stage, and I reviewed it. Because of the one-heavy-command rule, I ran every local cargo, gradle and vitest check and made every commit myself. Some review fixes (the page budget, the CSS filter rewrite, the fit, cache, referrer and refresh fixes) I wrote myself.
- **Emulator.** The installed `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture` is the CI APK at `db9f07e`. CI's debug key differs per run, so it was uninstalled and reinstalled. During this validation, taps from a faulty script landed in track A's app (`dev.exedev.emailos`): they opened one already-read conversation, collapsed a message and went back.

# ADR 0006: Displaying HTML mail

- Status: Accepted (implemented on `usable/html-reader`; see Implementation record)
- Date: 2026-11-21
- Track: C ("usable Android app" programme), branch `usable/html-reader`

## Context

The reader is plain text on every platform ([current status](../current-status.md),
line 58: "HTML mail rendering are not implemented"; ADR 0003 also excluded HTML
bodies from the phone layout). Most real mail is HTML, and some messages have no
`text/plain` part at all. ADR 0001 (line 46) allowed a plain-text reader first and
added: "HTML fidelity is not a reason to weaken isolation or sanitization." This ADR
proposes how to show HTML without weakening either.

### Where bodies come from today

- **Gmail parse.** `parse_thread` (`crates/mail-core/src/gmail/parse.rs:86`) reads a
  `threads.get?format=full` response. `parse_message` (`parse.rs:258`) takes the
  first literal `text/plain` part found by `find_plain_part` (`parse.rs:611`); an
  HTML-only payload yields `None`. Such a message is **dropped from the
  conversation** (`parse.rs:148-151`) and only counted in `unsupported_reason` as
  "N of M messages had no safe plain-text body" (`parse.rs:164-169`).
  `context_complete` becomes false.
- **Bounds.** One decoded MIME part ≤ 1 MiB (`MAX_PART_BODY_BYTES`, `parse.rs:13`),
  one text body ≤ 256 Ki chars (`MAX_MESSAGE_TEXT_CHARS`, `parse.rs:15`), payload
  depth ≤ 10 (`parse.rs:17`). One provider response ≤ 10 MiB (`auth.rs:484`). A sync
  page may retain ≤ 16 MiB of serialized conversations
  (`MAX_RETAINED_THREAD_BYTES_PER_PAGE`, `gmail/sync.rs:59`); exceeding it **fails
  the whole page** with `InvalidProviderResponse` (`sync.rs:978`, `sync.rs:2825`).
- **Charset.** The part is decoded strictly with its declared charset; lossy
  decoding rejects the body (`parse.rs:286-291`).
- **Inline content.** `has_omitted_inline_content` (`parse.rs:648`) discloses
  "additional inline MIME content is not displayed" when the selected text part is
  not the only inline content (for example a `multipart/related` with images).
- **Attachments.** `attachments::descriptors` (`crates/mail-core/src/attachments.rs:172`)
  records `messageId`, `attachmentId`, filename, MIME type and size for parts with a
  Gmail `attachmentId`, at most 32 (`attachments.rs:12`). It does not record
  `Content-ID`, so `cid:` references cannot be resolved today. Bytes are fetched on
  demand and bounded to 5 MiB (`attachments.rs:11`).
- **Cache.** `gmail_messages.body_text TEXT NOT NULL` is the only body column
  (`gmail/current-schema.sql:6`); schema is `gmail-migrations-9`
  (`gmail/store.rs:37`, `store_schema.rs:8`). The cache holds at most 100
  conversations (`DISCOVERY_CAP`, `gmail/store.rs:35`), evicted oldest first
  (`store/cache_rows.rs:249`). Operation and reminder snapshots store whole
  `Conversation` JSON (`gmail_operation_snapshots.snapshot_json`,
  `gmail_reminders.snapshot_json`).
- **Other users of `body_text`.** Row previews (`store/cache_rows.rs:466`), cached
  search (`search.rs:146`, `search.rs:198`), the read-only reply quote
  (`ReplyComposer.vue:149`), "Copy message text" (`ReaderView.vue:221`) and the
  Files and links list of plain-text URLs (`AttachmentChooser.vue:38-50`).
- **Synthetic provider.** The native fixture (ADR 0002) builds `GmailThread` values
  directly from seed data (`synthetic/provider.rs:185`); it does not go through
  `parse_thread`. Seed messages have one `body: &'static str`
  (`synthetic/data.rs:11-17`); 18 conversations, one synthetic `text/plain`
  attachment on each first message (`synthetic/provider.rs:224-233`). The browser
  preview has its own seed in `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts:287-321`, including
  three hostile-markup conversations that must render literally.

   layout and reading the document's scroll height, because engines disagree
   on how sizes of a zoomed root are reported (found by the phone-width

   fill it with HTML so that a later ordinary thread failed the page even
   without its HTML. HTML bodies and text derived from them now count toward a
   separate 8 MiB per page; past it a thread's HTML is recorded as too large

content.text:
I've fixed the macOS failures and committed them to `fix/webkit-html-frame` in two commits (`55d1459`, `bb3ae28`). Nothing is pushed and there's no PR yet. The sandbox is unchanged (still only `allow-same-origin`). I couldn't run WKWebView here, so the fix is tested in Chrome with WebKit's behaviour imitated, and the Mac recheck below is still needed.

## The fix

**How the frame picks its path.** When a frame loads, the app checks once per session whether its listeners on frame nodes actually run. On Chromium they do (Android and browser preview), and the old listener code is kept without any change. On WebKit they don't, so the frame switches to a path that needs no listener inside the frame (new file `src/lib/html-mail/frame-signals.ts`).

**Links (step 5).**
- Each link gets an `href` pointing to a spot inside the same document (`about:srcdoc#<nonce>-<i>`). It has to be the full `about:srcdoc` address, because a bare `#…` in a srcdoc frame would point at the app's own URL.
- A click, tap or Enter on a link is then the browser's own same-page jump, with no script. Nothing is fetched, and nothing scrolls because the jump target is a hidden element.
- That jump turns on a CSS rule that gives a hidden signal element a width. A ResizeObserver in the app sees the change, reads which link it was, resets the address, and opens the same confirmation as before.
- Mail can't add these elements (the sanitiser drops them; a new test covers this). Mail CSS can't fake a click either, because the app reads which link from the address, which only a real activation changes.

**Keys (step 6).** After a click inside the message, the app gives focus back to the reader once the mouse button is up. Focus stays in the frame in two cases: text is selected (so Copy works), or a link was reached with the keyboard (Tab, then Enter). The app starts checking when focus enters the frame or the mouse is pressed there, then every 100 ms while the frame has focus.

**Height fitting.** On WebKit the ResizeObserver also watches the images, replacing the image `load` listener.

**Probe (step 7).** The CSP check still requires a reported violation naming the image and `img-src`. It now accepts either the old event or a CSP report collected by a `ReportingObserver` created inside the frame, so it is not weaker. I first tried a same-origin image as a control, but the app's own CSP blocks it. The probe also tests the new link signal and reports whether the app's listeners run in frames (informational).

**Secondary issues.**
- **Logo (step 2):** fixed with your corrected bytes. Same 68 bytes and same pixel, and nothing else depended on the old bytes; the spike test now reads the fixture instead of a copy. The bad CRC didn't come from a tool or a text-encoding problem. Commit `80099ea` added the base64 by hand, and `ef bf 6b db` is not the replacement-character pattern (`ef bf bd`). A new core test checks the CRCs of every fixture PNG, and it fails on the old file.
- **Square images (step 1):** a failed image with `width` and `height` attributes now gets those proportions as an inline style. Loaded images and images still blocked behind Load images are left alone.

The ADR has a new implementation-record entry (12) describing this, plus notes on decisions 8 and 18 and the validation section.

## Known differences on WebKit
- Space on a focused link scrolls instead of opening it. Enter works.
- With text selected, or a link focused by keyboard, `j`/`k` wait until the next click.
- Each link activation adds one history entry inside the frame. The app doesn't use history, and the macOS webview has no back gesture.
- The console shows one "Blocked script execution" line per session, from the startup check.

## Tests
- **Imitating WebKit in Chrome:** a script added to the test page silences listeners on the mail frame the way WebKit does (`tests/rendered/webkit-listener-model.ts`). In that mode, 4 new reader tests pass:
  - real mouse clicks on the web link and the `mailto:` link, twice each, with the address and scroll unchanged;
  - Tab to a link, then Enter;
  - a click in the text, then `j` and `k`;
  - a drag selection that keeps focus, and image fitting after Load images.
- I checked that the keys test fails if focus is never given back.
- **Probe:** all checks pass in Chrome, both normally and in the WebKit imitation. In the imitation, the CSP check passes through the report signal alone.
- **Regressions:** the existing HTML reader rendered suite, desktop and phone, all pass, and so does the sanitiser rendered suite.
- **Unit and core checks:** frontend tests (2,308), typecheck, cargo fmt, clippy and `cargo test -p mail-core` all pass.

## What to recheck on the Mac
The imitation assumes WebKit still runs observer callbacks (ResizeObserver, ReportingObserver) for nodes inside the frame. The probe tests exactly that.
1. Run `pnpm tauri dev` on this branch and repeat steps 1–7.
2. Paste the new `FRAME_PROBE_SOURCE` from the branch. Every line should be PASS, especially:
   - "link signal seen by a parent ResizeObserver"
   - "link signal is same-document and scrolls nothing"
   - "remote image blocked by CSP"
   - "remote image violation signals" should show `listeners=false`, `via=report`
3. Step 5: click each link twice. Also Tab to a link and press Enter. The reader must not jump.
4. Step 6: click in the text, then press `j`/`k`/Escape. Then select some text, press Cmd+C and paste it somewhere.
5. Step 1: after Load images, the conv-19 header should be about 600×220. Step 2: the logo should be visible.

If "remote image blocked by CSP" fails only with `via=` empty, WebKit gives no listener-free CSP signal. The console's "Refused to load" line would then be the only evidence, and I'd need to rethink that check.

- Chromium still requires the violation event, and the line ends `via=event`.
- On WebKit the check is now structural (`via=structural`). All three must hold:
  - the frame carries the exact CSP meta;
  - a same-origin control image, `/src-tauri/icons/icon.png`, loads in the same kind of frame without the meta and is blocked with it;
  - the remote image did not load.
- I used this control rather than the image the policy allows (`data:`), because a `data:` image loads either way and can't tell a CSP block from a DNS failure. The control is allowed by the app CSP's `'self'`, and I checked that Vite dev serves it as `image/png` with status 200.
- In a production build there is no dev server, so no control image. There the line is labelled MANUAL and the console's "Refused to load" line is the proof.
- I removed the ReportingObserver path, since WebKit never delivers those reports.

**2. Broken images**
- Each fit now sets a pixel height from the `width`/`height` attributes, measured at zoom 1.
- It runs inside the existing fit, so it follows width changes through the observer that was already there. No new observer was added.
- Loaded images, images still blocked behind Load images, and images whose own style sets a height are left alone.
